name: ordewell
description: Plan once, run it across Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, and review one branch.
author: Alessandro Costanzo Ciano

scripts.build: tsup && vite build && node scripts/copy-skills.mjs && node scripts/verify-bundle.mjs && node ../../scripts/generate-third-party-notices.mjs vscode

ordewell.apiKey.description: Google Gemini API key (or set GEMINI_API_KEY env var)

ordewell.openAiApiKey.description: OpenRouter / OpenAI API key (or set OPENROUTER_API_KEY env var)

ordewell.aiProvider.description: Who plans: an API provider (google, openrouter, openai_compatible, or another vendor), or the id of a coding-agent runner installed on this machine, which plans on its own subscription with no API key. Auto-detected from the API keys you have set if left blank. The runner ids are the ones /runners lists; an unknown value is reported when it is set. Set it from the planner picker (/planner) rather than by hand.

ordewell.plannerThinkingEffort.description: Thinking effort for a coding-agent planner (e.g. low, medium, high) — pick from the agent's own model variants

ordewell.orchestratorModel.description: Main planning model (required. Use /planner or the Planner section to choose one)

ordewell.geminiModel.description: Gemini planning model (discovered automatically if empty)

ordewell.claudeCode.enabled.description: Enable Claude Code as a runner (legacy — use Ordewell: Toggle Runner instead)

ordewell.opencode.enabled.description: Enable OpenCode as a runner (legacy — use Ordewell: Toggle Runner instead)

ordewell.codex.enabled.description: Enable Codex as a runner (legacy — use Ordewell: Toggle Runner instead)

ordewell.enabledRunners.description: Retired: the enabled runners are saved in Ordewell's settings file, shared with the terminal UI. A value here is copied there once, then cleared.
ordewell.enabledRunners.deprecationMessage: The enabled runners are now saved in Ordewell's settings file, shared with the terminal UI. Use Ordewell: Toggle Runner, or /runners in the terminal UI.

ordewell.maxParallelSessions.description: How many AI tasks run at once (1 or more). A change applies to a run already going.

enumDescriptions: Follow the autonomy level: web reads run at both levels; otherwise Guarded asks you, and Full runs only the allowlist and asks nobody.
Ask you before any command, MCP tool, fetch or outside read the allowlist does not cover.
Run only what the allowlist covers and refuse the rest without asking.
Run everything except file writes, which are always refused.
ordewell.plannerApprovals.description: What the planner may run beyond read-only commands in the workspace. File writes are refused in every mode; changes belong to the plan's tasks.

ordewell.plannerAllowlist.description: Extra planner allowlist entries. A command rule such as "gh issue list" or "gcloud * * list" covers commands whose leading words match it; "mcp:find-*" covers MCP tools by name; "https://docs.example.com/*" or "/opt/data/*" covers fetches and outside reads; "web_search:<provider>" covers searches sent to one provider: anthropic (Claude Code), openai (Codex), opencode (OpenCode) or duckduckgo (Ordewell's own search). A leading "!" excludes, and an exclusion wins in every mode: "!web_search:*" turns every search off. To turn all web reads off, add "!web_search:*", "!https://*" and "!http://*", or set the web-read budget to 0. "mcp-server:<name>@<hash>" starts one exact MCP server a repository declares for the planner (the approval shows the entry); "!mcp-server:*" starts none.

ordewell.effectAllowlist.description: Script tasks the planner may run without asking you. A rule is matched against the whole command, every word in order and flags included: "git push origin feature/*" covers "git push origin feature/login", not the same push with "--force". "*" stands for one word, or inside a word for any run of characters, and a rule spells out its operation before any "*". A script task runs unasked only when every one of its commands is covered; a shell script, or a program named by its path, never is. The planner allowlist's "!" exclusions hold here too. There are no built-in rules.

ordewell.notifyCommand.description: A command to run when something new waits on you, such as a desktop notification or a message to a chat: the program, then each argument as its own item. It runs with no shell, in your home directory, with the escalation in the environment variables ORDEWELL_ESCALATION_ID, ORDEWELL_ESCALATION_KIND, ORDEWELL_ESCALATION_TASK and ORDEWELL_ESCALATION_REASON. It runs once for each escalation and never affects a run. A user setting only: a workspace's value is ignored.

ordewell.plannerWebReadBudget.description: How many fetches and web searches the planner may make in one turn. Past it, web reads are refused and the planner says so. 0 turns web reads off.

ordewell.plannerAllowlistDefaults.description: Include Ordewell's built-in allowlist of read-only commands (GitHub, GitLab, Azure, Google Cloud, AWS, Kubernetes, containers, installed packages and more) and read-only MCP tools.

ordewell.plannerNativeShell.description: Let a harness planner (Claude Code, OpenCode) use its own shell beside run_command, with writes confined to a scratch folder and the user's credential stores out of reach. Only offered for versions checked live: Claude Code 2.1.304–2.1.x and OpenCode 2.0.32–2.0.x on macOS. Other versions and platforms, and OpenCode 1.x, keep run_command alone. The shell keeps whatever network its harness gives it. Codex already has its own shell, so this changes nothing for it. A user setting: a workspace cannot set it.

ordewell.worktreeIsolation.description: In a git repository, run each AI task in its own worktree and integrate the results on a per-run branch. Turn off to run every task in the shared workspace.

ordewell.worktreeSetupCommand.description: Command run in each new task worktree instead of symlinking node_modules, .env files and agent config from the main worktree. It runs in every repository of a multi-repo folder; where it fails, that repository gets the default links instead, with a warning.

ordewell.workspaceRepos.description: In a folder that is not itself a git repository, the repositories to isolate together, as paths relative to the workspace. When set, exactly these are isolated, replacing the automatic pick of the repositories directly inside the folder; list one there too to keep it. Needed for repositories nested deeper than one level.

ordewell.worktreeLinks.description: Extra paths or globs, relative to each repository root, linked from the real repository into every task worktree where they exist — for gitignored local state such as *.tfstate or .terraform/.

ordewell.conflictRepairAttempts.description: When a finished task's work conflicts with what has landed since, how many times Ordewell asks the task's own runner to merge the latest work into its worktree and resolve the conflict before leaving it for you. 0 turns conflict repair off, so every conflict waits for you.
